cards.title: Straw phonation
instructions: Hum a steady note through a narrow straw. Lips sealed, jaw loose.
Glide slowly up and down your range. It should feel almost effortless.
If it feels like work, you are still pushing — go quieter, not harder.
TRANSFER: straw out, and say one ordinary sentence with that same easy feeling. This is the part that counts.

cards.title: Straw into water
instructions: Straw into about two inches of water. Hum through it.
Keep the bubbles steady and even — evenness is the goal, not duration.
TRANSFER: straw out, one ordinary sentence, same easy feeling.

cards.title: Humming warm-up
instructions: Lips closed, teeth slightly apart, jaw loose.
Hum a comfortable low note. Buzz on the lips and nose, not in the throat.
If you feel it in the throat, go quieter. This drill takes work off the throat.
TRANSFER: open into a sentence, keeping the buzz alive through the words.

cards.title: Lip trill
instructions: Loose lips, let them flutter on a steady note — a motorbike sound.
If they stop fluttering you are blowing too hard. Less air, not more.
Trill up and down a comfortable range.
TRANSFER: trill, then slide straight into a sentence without changing the effort.

cards.title: The long Z
instructions: Steady 'zzzzz', low and easy. This one your own measurements already proved works — your /z/ ran 25 seconds.
Keep it even. The moment it gets louder or rougher, you are pushing.
TRANSFER: 'zzzz' straight into 'zeeee-I looked at the numbers again this morning.'

cards.title: Yawn-sigh
instructions: Begin a real yawn. Feel the throat open into a wide, cool space.
Before it finishes, sigh out on 'haaah' holding that open feeling.
Six times. That dropped, open position is the target for everything else.
TRANSFER: one sentence spoken while holding that same posture.

cards.title: The reset sigh
instructions: In through the nose for four, then a short second sip on top.
Long slow sigh out through the mouth for eight, jaw loose. Six rounds.
Use this in the two minutes before you have to speak to a room.
TRANSFER: finish on a sigh that turns into your first sentence.

cards.title: Low and slow
instructions: Say this at half the speed that feels right: 'I looked at the numbers again this morning.'
Again, quieter, letting the last word land fully. Four times, each quieter than felt comfortable.
It will feel absurdly slow to you and completely normal to a listener. That gap is the correction.
TRANSFER: now say something of your own at that same speed and volume.

cards.title: Ribs, not shoulders
instructions: Hands on the sides of your lower ribs, fingers pointing forward.
Breathe in — the ribs widen sideways. If the shoulders rise instead, that is chest breathing.
Chest breathing is why the volume ends up coming from your throat. Ten slow breaths.
TRANSFER: one sentence on a rib breath, shoulders still.

cards.title: The open hold
instructions: One comfortable breath — not a maximal one.
Hold an open 'aaah' at your NORMAL speaking volume, as steadily as you can.
Do not push for a record. This measures the habit as it actually is.
Log the seconds. 15 today, 25 by week twelve — and it moves because the habit moves, not because your lungs do.
